Nothing here destroys anything. This is the register and its transition rules;
`transitionProblems` decides whether a move is permitted and no function performs one. §14.3's
own text says of hardware "do not direct Claude to physically destroy hardware", and the same
restraint applies to every other disposition.

## The state machine (EXT-120-001)

§14.2's chain, 11 states:

`DISCOVERED → DEPENDENCY_MAPPED → RETIREMENT_APPROVED → CHANGE_FROZEN → READ_ONLY → ARCHIVING → ACCESS_REVOKING → DESTROYING → VERIFIED → CONTRACT_CLOSED → RETIRED_TOMBSTONE`

Its 5 control states are flags held ALONGSIDE a lifecycle state, not
positions on the chain — an asset under legal hold is still at whatever state it reached, and
modelling the hold as a state would lose that position the moment the hold landed.

| Control | Blocks advancing out of | Because |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LEGAL_HOLD` | ACCESS_REVOKING | §14.3: "Reconciliation and record/legal-hold sign-offs pass." A hold is the record surviving the system, so the asset may be archived and made read-only and may not be destroyed. |
| `RETENTION_ONLY` | ACCESS_REVOKING | §14.3: "Backups, replicas, logs, caches, endpoints, snapshots, archives, and disaster-recovery copies follow approved disposition." An asset retained for a retention schedule is kept deliberately; destroying it is the schedule not being followed. |
| `BLOCKED_DEPENDENCY` | DEPENDENCY_MAPPED | §14.3: "Downstream integrations/reports/users are migrated or formally retired." Approving retirement while something still depends on it approves the outage rather than the retirement. |
| `ROLLBACK_WINDOW` | READ_ONLY | §14.3: "Source becomes read-only for a defined rollback/reference period with monitored access." Archiving away from a source inside its own rollback window removes the fallback the window exists to be. |
| `ABORTED` | _any state_ | §14.2 lists ABORTED among the control states. A retirement somebody stopped does not continue advancing; it stops where it was, so the decision to resume is visible as a decision. |

| Attempt | Asset | Move | Controls | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `archive-after-window` | `legacy-shared-drive` | READ_ONLY → ARCHIVING | — | permitted |
| `archive-inside-rollback-window` | `legacy-sis` | READ_ONLY → ARCHIVING | ROLLBACK_WINDOW | `blocked-by-control-state` |
| `destroy-under-legal-hold` | `legacy-records-archive` | ACCESS_REVOKING → DESTROYING | LEGAL_HOLD | `blocked-by-control-state` |
| `destroy-under-retention` | `legacy-nightly-backup` | ACCESS_REVOKING → DESTROYING | RETENTION_ONLY | `blocked-by-control-state` |
| `approve-with-blocked-dependency` | `legacy-sftp-account` | DEPENDENCY_MAPPED → RETIREMENT_APPROVED | BLOCKED_DEPENDENCY | `blocked-by-control-state` |
| `skip-to-verified` | `legacy-shared-drive` | READ_ONLY → VERIFIED | — | `skipped-states` |
| `resurrect-a-destroyed-asset` | `legacy-scanner` | DESTROYING → READ_ONLY | — | `backwards-transition` |
| `advance-while-aborted` | `legacy-event-queue` | DISCOVERED → DEPENDENCY_MAPPED | ABORTED | `blocked-by-control-state` |

The chain's own next step is derived, not listed twice: `nextState("READ_ONLY")` is `ARCHIVING` and `nextState("RETIRED_TOMBSTONE")` is `null` — the end of the chain, which is a different answer from an unknown state.

## Refusals

Each row mutates the estate above in exactly ONE way and reports what refused it. One at a
time because two mutations can mask each other, and a scenario that trips three rules proves
that something refused it rather than that this rule did.

| Scenario | Requirement | Mutation | Refused by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind-not-surveyed` | EXT-120-001 | The service-account row removed, with no survey saying there are none. | `kind-not-surveyed` |
| `survey-unreasoned` | EXT-120-001 | The same absence declared surveyed, with no reason for the emptiness. | `survey-unreasoned` |
| `fact-missing` | EXT-120-001 | An asset with no recorded owner. | `fact-missing` |
| `dangling-dependency` | EXT-120-001 | A dependency on something outside the inventory. | `dangling-dependency` |
| `dependency-unmapped` | EXT-120-001 | An asset past DISCOVERED with no dependency list at all — not an empty one, none. | `dependency-unmapped` |
| `dependency-cycle` | EXT-120-001 | Two assets that depend on each other, so no retirement order exists. | `dependency-cycle` |
| `duplicate-asset` | EXT-120-001 | One thing inventoried twice. | `duplicate-asset` |
| `unknown-kind` | EXT-120-001 | A kind invented in the register, which no §14.3 gate was written for. | `unknown-kind` |
| `control-state-as-lifecycle-state` | EXT-120-001 | LEGAL_HOLD used as a position on the chain rather than a flag beside it. | `control-state-is-not-a-lifecycle-state` |
